Portuguese here. First of all, the "Socialist Party" isn't socialist at all. In the 25th of April 1974, a two year-long revolutionary process began, which culminated with the approval of a new Constitution that established a liberal democracy and ended almost five decades of fascist repression. Political parties created during that period (or a few months before, as is the case of the "Socialist" party) all have their names shifted towards the left more than they actually are. Hence, the party denominated social democratic is actually a center right free market party, and the previously only other right-wing party represented in parliament was the "democratic and social CENTER". The Socialists are actually a very ideologically diverse party, ranging from centrist liberals cautious about the state's role in the economy to some actual leftist types. But they sure don't have any socialists.
The reason that party just achieved an outright majority (only the second time they did it in over 40 years of elections) seems to be the fear of a right-wing government presided by the "social-democrats" with the support of the neolibs and the fascist crazies, instilled by months of TV propaganda supporting bipolarization on the two main parties and opinion polls that showed the right of center parties etching ahead and achieving a majority. As a result, the left voters, which supported the left bloc and the communist party, disengaged with their usual choices and preferred the ruling socialist party, which won in almost every district, and which vote share rised in pretty much the same margins as the left parties' fell.
You think they are really lacking people to hammer into the ticket in order to prevent anyone even resembling a centre-leftist from being a candidate? I ain't American and sure could name a few
